programs.nl_rule:
In the input, you should see...a grid with colored pixels scattered. Some of the pixels are touching other pixels {on sides/or corners} while some are singletons, not touching any pixels

The output grid size...The output grid size does not change. It is the same as the input

To make the output, you have to...copy the input grid, identify which pixels are connected or touching any other and change background colors of single pixels to the background color or black. Done

content.text:
Let me understand the rule from the verifier.

`objects(I, F, T, T)`: univalued=False, diagonal=True, without_bg=True. So objects are connected components using 8-connectivity (diagonal=True), not restricted to same value, excluding background.

Wait, univalued=False means objects are formed by non-background pixels regardless of color, connected via 8-connectivity.

Then `sizefilter(x0, ONE)` filters objects of size 1 — singletons (isolated non-background pixels).

`merge(x1)` merges them into a set of cells (objects are cells). Actually objects returns frozenset of (val, loc) tuples. merge flattens... `merge` does `type(containers)(e for c in containers for e in c)`. So x1 is frozenset of objects, each object is frozenset of (val,loc). merge gives frozenset of (val,loc). Then `cover(I, x2)` fills those indices with mostcolor(grid) which is background (0).

So the rule: find non-background pixels that are isolated (no neighbor, including diagonals, of non-background color). Set them to background.

Wait, background is mostcolor of grid. So the single pixels that are isolated get changed to background.

So essentially: any non-background cell that has no adjacent non-background cell (8-connectivity) becomes background.

Note: since univalued=False, objects merge different colors that touch. So a singleton is a connected component of size 1.

Important: the "background" color is mostcolor. In these examples it's 0.

Let me verify with the teacher example. Grid 16x8. Color 9 pixels.

Row0: cols5,6 = 9,9. These touch each other → object size 2, keep.
Row1: col0=9 (isolated? check neighbors: row0 col0=0, row0 col1=0, row1 col1=0, row2 col0=0... isolated → removed). col4=9: check neighbors: row0 col3=0,col4=0,col5=9 → adjacent to 9 at (0,5)? Diagonal: (0,3),(0,4),(0,5). (0,5) is 9 → touches → keep.
Row2: col3=9: neighbors (1,2)=0,(1,3)=0,(1,4)=9 → touches → keep.
Row3: col2=9,col3=9. (3,2) touches (3,3) and (2,3)? (2,3)=9 diagonal → keep. Both kept.
Row4: col2=9: neighbors (3,1)=0,(3,2)=9 → keep. col7=9: isolated? neighbors row3 col6,7, row4 col6, row5 col6,7 all 0 → isolated → removed.
Row5: col3=9: neighbors (4,2)=9? (3,2)? diag (4,2)=9 yes → keep.
Row6: col0=9 isolated? neighbors (5,-1),(5,0),(5,1),(6,1),(7,0),(7,1) all 0 → removed. col2=9: neighbors (5,1),(5,2),(5,3)=9 → keep. col6=9 isolated → removed.
Row7: col4=9 isolated? neighbors row6 col3,4,5, row7 col3,5, row8 col3,4,5 = all 0 → removed.
Row8: col1=9: neighbors row7 col0,1,2 all 0, row8 col0,2=0, row9 col0=0,col1=9 → touches → keep.
Row9: col1=9: touches row8 col1=9 → keep. col5=9 isolated → removed.
Row10: col1=9: touches row9 col1 → keep.
Row11: col0=9: neighbors row10 col0,1=9 (col1 is 9) → keep? row10 col1=9 yes diagonal → keep. col7=9 isolated? neighbors row10 col6,7, row11 col6, row12 col6,7 = 0 → removed.
Row12: col1=9: neighbor row11 col0=9 diagonal → keep.
Row13: col0,col1=9,9: touch each other → keep.
Row15: col4=9 isolated → removed.

Now output row1: col0 removed (0), col4 kept. Matches. Good.

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Show the Student a labeled input-output pair that you authored. If your output matches the rule, the pair is shown and you receive a success acknowledgement only. If it does not match, the pair is not shown and you receive the gold output so you can correct it.

tools.name: show_transformed_input

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Provide only an input grid. The environment applies the verifier and shows the resulting gold input-output pair to the student.

tools.name: query_student

tools.description: Probe the student with an input of your choice. You receive the student's predicted output, the gold output, and whether they matched. The student does not see the gold pair unless you later show it with show_example or show_transformed_input.

tools.name: start_exam
tools.description: End teaching and send the student to the exam: they must solve held-out generator inputs (unseen in demonstrations or probes) with the history so far. No further teaching after this.
